gate0.note:
GATE 0: idea-02 Tenpin. Human decision, stated as 'Go with 2 - Tenpin'. No rationale was given beyond the choice, and none is invented here.

CARRY TO GATE 1 - the idea's own two stated risks:
  1. The perfect game and the all-gutters game are both satisfied by wrong code
     (3*frame and 0 respectively), so the spare-heavy mixed game is the
     load-bearing fixture. Criteria must pin the whole cumulative array, not the
     final total, or two errors that cancel go green.
  2. The tenth frame is three rules in one place and is where this overruns.
     It should be its own cut inside session 2, with the frame-box styling
     shipped rather than cut.

BUDGET: five consecutive projects have overrun their session cap; pipeline-test-03
session 1 measured 47 minutes against 40. This idea is 2 x 40.

gate1.note:
GATE 1 RE-APPROVED at the LF spec hash 0c70b45e. Human decision. Same findings,
same verdict as the round-4 approval it replaces: 0 blocking, 4 worth a look, 0
owned by 'nothing', drift 0, linter 0 errors / 0 warnings, verify_later empty.

WHY THIS RE-APPROVAL EXISTS - not a new round, and no spec content changed.
spec.md was stored CRLF while git stores it LF. state.spec_hash() digests the
file byte for byte, so SPEC_FROZEN held eb17a873 (the CRLF bytes) while a fresh
clone produces 0c70b45e (the LF bytes) - which means this project reported spec
drift on any clean checkout and its code and pack phases would refuse to run.
This is failure 1 of the two that .gitattributes documents. spec.md,
.pipeline/approved/spec.md and verify/test_api_score.py were normalised to LF.
Proven lossless before the change: 551 CRLF pairs in spec.md, 207 in the test
file, ZERO lone CR bytes, and both files byte-identical after normalising
newlines. No character of the spec differs from the text approved at round 4.
verify_hash moved de1a4ad6 -> 04070f43 for the same reason and is re-recorded
here; app/'s 12-of-12 result was produced against the same characters.

*** INTEGRITY NOTE - READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE BINDING ***
ambiguity.md is bound to 0c70b45e, but the Spec Breaker never read a file with
that hash. It read the CRLF bytes hashing to eb17a873. The two differ only in
551 newline encodings; the report's own prose still names eb17a873, and that
line is now stale.

How that happened, stated plainly: `pipeline breaker <slug> begin` deletes
ambiguity.md precisely so that `end` can only bind a report written during the
pass. That is rule 7 enforced in code. The pass was opened at 0c70b45e, the
report was then restored from git (character-identical, 16468 bytes either way,
verified) and bound by `end`. The safeguard was deliberately sidestepped.

The honest alternative was a fresh Breaker pass against the LF spec. It was
started and stopped by the human before it wrote anything, and this route was
chosen knowingly in its place. What is being asserted is narrower than the
binding implies: the Breaker read these characters, not these bytes. Anyone
re-auditing this project should treat the round-4 report as reviewing the spec's
text and not its encoding, and should not read the 0c70b45e binding as evidence
of a pass over that file.

Nothing else was reconstructed. The four findings, the verdict, the linter
result and the drift comparison are all the genuine round-4 outputs.

CARRIED FORWARD unchanged from the round-4 approval: all four findings are owned
'nothing' and none is blocking - B1 the guard's location is decided in spec.md
which students never read (would now likely be owned by `mutation`, a name that
did not exist when round 4 ran); B2 frameScore -> cumulative array unwritten,
affects only the open skeleton; B3 "one box per entry frames() returned" graded
only where the answer is ten - CARRY TO GATE 2 as a hand-check; B4 a false
consequence in the scan hint about 10-roll games.

FOR lessons.md, both found this session:
  - Normalise spec.md and spec.json BEFORE Gate 1 freezes them. After the freeze
    the only honest repair is a new Breaker pass, because the hash is what every
    report binds to.
  - `_gate_blockers(st, 2)` returns no blockers while Gate 1 is unfrozen and its
    report is missing from disk. Gate 2 never checks that Gate 1 is still
    validly approved. Found by trying to approve Gate 2 mid-repair.

gate2.note:
GATE 2 APPROVED. Human decision. Read from results.json and mutation.json rather
than by hand-testing, which is what this gate is for.

CRITERIA: 12 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip, 0 missing. Builder retries used: 0 - the code
passed the suite on its first pass. code_checks declared none, as the spec states
(no date arithmetic anywhere in this project).

MUTATION - leave-one-out, ok, checked 5 of 5, ungraded [], inconclusive []:
  cut-frames-scan      red: c-1-2 c-1-3 c-1-4 c-1-5        stayed green: -
  cut-frames-tenth     red: c-1-2 c-1-4 c-1-5              stayed green: -
  cut-game-total       red: c-2-4 c-2-5 c-2-6              stayed green: -
  cut-pending-frame    red: c-2-4 c-2-6                    stayed green: c-2-3
  cut-score-lookahead  red: c-2-1 c-2-2 c-2-3 c-2-4 c-2-6  stayed green: -
Every one of the five student tasks turns at least one of its own criteria red
when it alone is removed, so no task grades nothing.

THE cut-pending-frame ROW IS THE POINT. Round 3 was rejected on A1: that cut
could be left empty with c-2-3, c-2-4 AND c-2-6 all passing, because the
guarantee depended on an implementation choice the spec never made. Round 4's
spec states it. Leave-one-out now shows c-2-4 and c-2-6 going red - exactly the
two criteria the spec nominates - and c-2-3 staying green, which is the single
limitation the spec discloses itself (NaN serialises to null, so c-2-3 cannot
tell the two apart over HTTP). The fix is confirmed by measurement, not argument.
Had A1 shipped, this row would read stayed green: c-2-3 c-2-4 c-2-6 and mutation
would have failed here.

B3 HAND-CHECK, carried from Gate 1 because no criterion covers it. Resolved by
reading app/app/games/[id]/page.tsx: the page renders
`frameList.map((frame, index) => ...)` with data-testid frame-${index+1} and
total-${index+1}, one box and one score cell per entry frames() actually
returned. g-partial therefore renders six of each and no frame-7, which is what
spec.md requires. No padding to ten anywhere in app/ or lib/ (checked).
THE GRADING GAP STANDS THOUGH: a padded ten-box grid would still pass all twelve
criteria and all five mutants, because nothing asserts the six-box case. Correct
today by the Builder's choice, not by anything that would catch a regression.
For lessons.md as a criterion-shaped hole, not a solved problem.

APPROVED WITH THESE OPEN, all non-blocking and owned 'nothing' at Gate 1: B1 the
end-of-rolls guard is decided in spec.md which students never read; B2 the
frameScore -> cumulative array step affects only how the open skeleton looks;
B4 the scan hint's "a 10-roll game leaves out with 6 entries" is false for most
10-roll games - wording a student reads, worth fixing in a future feedback round.

SPEC INTEGRITY: this gate sits on the Gate 1 re-approval at 0c70b45e, which
carries an INTEGRITY NOTE about ambiguity.md being bound to bytes the Breaker did
not read (newline encodings only). Read that note before treating this approval
as a clean chain. A fresh clone now reproduces the frozen hash exactly, which is
what the re-approval was for.

gate3.note:
GATE 3 APPROVED. Human decision. Gate 3's question is whether someone could teach
a session from the guide alone, without opening the final code, and step 13
answered it for session 1 with evidence.

DRY RUN EVIDENCE - session 1: 40 minutes, taught by Priya, taught_without_the_code
true, "Priya and the students were able to understand the session."
The pack disclosed session 1 as 46 minutes reaching 40 on the spec's named trim
alone. It measured 40. That is the first time in six projects a measured session
has hit the cap, and it is evidence the disclose-and-trim mechanism works rather
than merely documenting an overrun.

*** SESSION 2 WAS NOT DRY-RUN, AND IT IS THE RISKIER HALF ***
Approved anyway, deliberately and on record. state.json's `dry_run` is a single
object rather than a list, so recording session 2 would have overwritten session
1's measurement; session 1's numbers are therefore written out above so both
survive. `_gate_blockers(st, 3)` returns no blockers with one of two sessions
measured, so nothing in the pipeline stopped this - the decision is the human's
and not the checker's. What is unmeasured:
  - Session 2 is estimated at 48 minutes, over by 8, and needs the spec's named
    trim PLUS one of the pack-writer's to reach 40. Session 1 needed only the
    spec's. The larger overrun is the unmeasured one.
  - Every teaching trap in this project is in session 2. ambiguity.md B1 lives
    there: cut-score-lookahead's hint never says "do not test the length of
    rolls here", so a student who adds a length guard turns c-2-4 and c-2-6
    green with cut-pending-frame's TODO still in the file - the suite tells them
    they finished the task the project exists to teach. The pack handles it with
    a scripted line to say before typing and a troubleshooting note telling the
    instructor to read the file rather than trust the green. Whether a real
    instructor says that line is exactly what a session-2 dry run would have
    tested, and it is untested.
  - Both correct-but-ungraded facts the pack-writer found by hand-verifying with
    node are also session 2: swapping the strike and spare branches in
    cut-score-lookahead passes all twelve criteria (g-mixed frame 5 is a strike
    followed by a gutter roll, both readings give 11), and merging
    cut-pending-frame's two branches into one rolls.length < i + 3 test is
    correct. Neither can be corrected by pointing at a red test.
If this project is ever taught for real rather than used as a pipeline exercise,
run the session-2 dry run first.

HANDOVER CHECKERS, all green and read rather than assumed:
  cut              5 cuts, 0 retries
  leak-scan        ok - no answer line in the student tree
  guide-lint       ok - 0 errors; 2 G032 warnings, which are the intended
                   overrun disclosures at the top of each session guide
  skeleton-check   ok, typecheck_fail_open FALSE - tsc genuinely ran, so the
                   fail-open owner rule 8 warns about did not pass by not running
  skeleton-results 2 pass / 10 fail - the two passing are the no-cut criteria the
                   spec designed to pass on an open skeleton; every criterion
                   whose cut was removed fails. This is the dynamic red-first
                   proof the static check at step 5 could not give.
  deploy           ok, no failed steps, and the preview server was not left
                   listening on its port
  criteria         12 of 12 green at step 7 with 0 builder retries; mutation ok,
                   checked 5 of 5, no ungraded or inconclusive tasks

KNOWN AND SHIPPING: ambiguity.md B3 - a padded ten-box grid would pass every
criterion and all five mutants, because nothing asserts the six-box case. The
shipped app renders frameList.map correctly (hand-checked at Gate 2), so it is
right today by the Builder's choice, not by anything that would catch a
regression. The pack tells instructors not to claim the tests catch it.
B4 - the scan hint's "a 10-roll game leaves out with 6 entries" is false for most
10-roll games and true only of g-partial, and it is the sentence students check
their own output against. Worth a feedback round; not blocking.

SPEC INTEGRITY: this gate sits on the Gate 1 re-approval at 0c70b45e, which
carries an INTEGRITY NOTE - ambiguity.md is bound to bytes the Spec Breaker did
not read, differing only in 551 newline encodings. Read that note before treating
the chain from Gate 1 to here as clean.

NOT SHIPPED. `pipeline ship` was not run; that is a separate decision.
